audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Jacob's departure, Laban's changing wages, dream revelation, household gods, Rachel's concealment, covenant heap, Mizpah/Galeed naming, and oath boundaries.

verses.restored: Jacob heard the words of Laban’s sons, saying, Jacob has taken all that was our father’s, and from what was our father’s he has made all this weight/wealth.

familiar.text: And he heard the words of Laban's sons, saying, Jacob hath taken away all that was our father's...

modern.text: Now Jacob heard that Laban’s sons were saying, “Jacob has taken away all that belonged to our father and built all this wealth at our father’s expense.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֗ע אֶת דִּבְרֵ֤י בְנֵֽי לָבָן֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לָקַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֵ֖ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֑ינוּ וּמֵאֲשֶׁ֣ר לְאָבִ֔ינוּ עָשָׂ֕ה אֵ֥ת כָּל הַכָּבֹ֖ד הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Jacob saw the face of Laban, and behold, it was not toward him as before.

familiar.text: And Jacob beheld the countenance of Laban...

modern.text: And Jacob saw from the countenance of Laban that his attitude toward him had changed.

original.text: וַיַּ֥רְא יַעֲקֹ֖ב אֶת פְּנֵ֣י לָבָ֑ן וְהִנֵּ֥ה אֵינֶ֛נּוּ עִמּ֖וֹ כִּתְמ֥וֹל שִׁלְשֽׁוֹם

verses.restored: The Eternal said to Jacob, Return to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.

familiar.text: And the LORD said unto Jacob, Return unto the land of thy fathers...

notes.title: Return command
notes.body: The Bethel promise of return now becomes a command.

modern.text: Then the LORD said to Jacob, “Go back to the land of your fathers and to your kindred, and I will be with you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יְהוָה֙ אֶֽל יַעֲקֹ֔ב שׁ֛וּב אֶל אֶ֥רֶץ אֲבוֹתֶ֖יךָ וּלְמוֹלַדְתֶּ֑ךָ וְאֶֽהְיֶ֖ה עִמָּֽךְ

verses.restored: Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field, to his flock.

familiar.text: And Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field unto his flock,

modern.text: So Jacob sent word and called Rachel and Leah to the field where his flocks were,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיִּקְרָ֖א לְרָחֵ֣ל וּלְלֵאָ֑ה הַשָּׂדֶ֖ה אֶל צֹאנֽוֹ

verses.restored: He said to them, I see your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before, but the Divine of my father has been with me.

familiar.text: And said unto them, I see your father's countenance...

modern.text: and he told them, “I can see from your father’s countenance that his attitude toward me has changed; but the God of my father has been with me.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ן רֹאֶ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ אֶת פְּנֵ֣י אֲבִיכֶ֔ן כִּֽי אֵינֶ֥נּוּ אֵלַ֖י כִּתְמֹ֣ל שִׁלְשֹׁ֑ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֣י אָבִ֔י הָיָ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי

verses.restored: You know that with all my strength I have served your father.

familiar.text: And ye know that with all my power I have served your father.

modern.text: You know that I have served your father with all my strength.

original.text: וְאַתֵּ֖נָה יְדַעְתֶּ֑ן כִּ֚י בְּכָל כֹּחִ֔י עָבַ֖דְתִּי אֶת אֲבִיכֶֽן

verses.restored: Yet your father has deceived me and changed my wages ten times, but the Divine did not allow him to do harm to me.

familiar.text: And your father hath deceived me, and changed my wages ten times...

modern.text: And although he has cheated me and changed my wages ten times, God has not allowed him to harm me.

original.text: וַאֲבִיכֶן֙ הֵ֣תֶל בִּ֔י וְהֶחֱלִ֥ף אֶת מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֣רֶת מֹנִ֑ים וְלֹֽא נְתָנ֣וֹ אֱלֹהִ֔ים לְהָרַ֖ע עִמָּדִֽי

verses.restored: If he said, The speckled shall be your wages, then all the flock bore speckled; and if he said, The striped shall be your wages, then all the flock bore striped.

familiar.text: If he said thus, The speckled shall be thy wages...

modern.text: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore speckled offspring. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then the whole flock bore streaked offspring.

original.text: אִם כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר נְקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל הַצֹּ֖אן נְקֻדִּ֑ים וְאִם כֹּ֣ה יֹאמַ֗ר עֲקֻדִּים֙ יִהְיֶ֣ה שְׂכָרֶ֔ךָ וְיָלְד֥וּ כָל הַצֹּ֖אן עֲקֻדִּֽים

verses.restored: So the Divine has taken away the livestock of your father and given them to me.

familiar.text: Thus God hath taken away the cattle of your father, and given them to me.

modern.text: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock and given them to me.

original.text: וַיַּצֵּ֧ל אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶת מִקְנֵ֥ה אֲבִיכֶ֖ם וַיִּתֶּן לִֽי

verses.restored: At the time the flock was breeding, I lifted my eyes and saw in a dream: behold, the male goats mounting the flock were striped, speckled, and mottled.

familiar.text: And it came to pass at the time that the cattle conceived...

modern.text: When the flocks were breeding, I saw in a dream that the streaked, spotted, and speckled males were mating with the females.

original.text: וַיְהִ֗י בְּעֵת֙ יַחֵ֣ם הַצֹּ֔אן וָאֶשָּׂ֥א עֵינַ֛י וָאֵ֖רֶא בַּחֲל֑וֹם וְהִנֵּ֤ה הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּֽים

verses.restored: The messenger of the Divine said to me in the dream, Jacob. I said, Here I am.

familiar.text: And the angel of God spake unto me in a dream, saying, Jacob...

modern.text: In that dream the angel of God said to me, ‘Jacob!’ And I replied, ‘Here I am.’

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר אֵלַ֜י מַלְאַ֧ךְ הָאֱלֹהִ֛ים בַּחֲל֖וֹם יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב וָאֹמַ֖ר הִנֵּֽנִי

verses.restored: He said, Lift your eyes now and see: all the male goats mounting the flock are striped, speckled, and mottled, for I have seen all that Laban is doing to you.

familiar.text: And he said, Lift up now thine eyes, and see...

modern.text: ‘Look up,’ he said, ‘and see that all the males that are mating with the flock are streaked, spotted, or speckled; for I have seen all that Laban has done to you.

original.text: וַיֹּ֗אמֶר שָׂא נָ֨א עֵינֶ֤יךָ וּרְאֵה֙ כָּל הָֽעַתֻּדִים֙ הָעֹלִ֣ים עַל הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּבְרֻדִּ֑ים כִּ֣י רָאִ֔יתִי אֵ֛ת כָּל אֲשֶׁ֥ר לָבָ֖ן עֹ֥שֶׂה לָּֽךְ

verses.restored: I am the Divine of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar and where you vowed a vow to me. Now rise, go out from this land, and return to the land of your kindred.

familiar.text: I am the God of Bethel, where thou anointedst the pillar...

modern.text: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed the pillar and made a solemn vow to Me. Now get up and leave this land at once, and return to your native land.’”

original.text: אָנֹכִ֤י הָאֵל֙ בֵּֽית אֵ֔ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר מָשַׁ֤חְתָּ שָּׁם֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָדַ֥רְתָּ לִּ֛י שָׁ֖ם נֶ֑דֶר עַתָּ֗ה ק֥וּם צֵא֙ מִן הָאָ֣רֶץ הַזֹּ֔את וְשׁ֖וּב אֶל אֶ֥רֶץ מוֹלַדְתֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: Rachel and Leah answered and said to him, Is there still any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?

familiar.text: And Rachel and Leah answered and said unto him, Is there yet any portion...

modern.text: And Rachel and Leah replied, “Do we have any portion or inheritance left in our father’s house?

original.text: וַתַּ֤עַן רָחֵל֙ וְלֵאָ֔ה וַתֹּאמַ֖רְנָה ל֑וֹ הַע֥וֹד לָ֛נוּ חֵ֥לֶק וְנַחֲלָ֖ה בְּבֵ֥ית אָבִֽינוּ

verses.restored: Are we not counted by him as foreigners? For he has sold us, and has completely eaten up our silver.

familiar.text: Are we not counted of him strangers? for he hath sold us...

notes.title: Sold us
notes.body: Rachel and Leah interpret Laban’s treatment as exploitation rather than fatherly provision.

modern.text: Are we not regarded by him as outsiders? Not only has he sold us, but he has certainly squandered what was paid for us.

original.text: הֲל֧וֹא נָכְרִיּ֛וֹת נֶחְשַׁ֥בְנוּ ל֖וֹ כִּ֣י מְכָרָ֑נוּ וַיֹּ֥אכַל גַּם אָכ֖וֹל אֶת כַּסְפֵּֽנוּ

verses.restored: All the wealth that the Divine has taken from our father belongs to us and to our children. Now then, all that the Divine has said to you, do.

familiar.text: For all the riches which God hath taken from our father...

modern.text: Surely all the wealth that God has taken away from our father belongs to us and to our children. So do whatever God has told you.”

original.text: כִּ֣י כָל הָעֹ֗שֶׁר אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִצִּ֤יל אֱלֹהִים֙ מֵֽאָבִ֔ינוּ לָ֥נוּ ה֖וּא וּלְבָנֵ֑ינוּ וְעַתָּ֗ה כֹּל֩ אֲשֶׁ֨ר אָמַ֧ר אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֵלֶ֖יךָ עֲשֵֽׂה

verses.restored: Jacob rose and lifted his children and his women onto the camels.

familiar.text: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives upon camels;

modern.text: Then Jacob got up and put his children and his wives on camels,

original.text: וַיָּ֖קָם יַעֲקֹ֑ב וַיִּשָּׂ֛א אֶת בָּנָ֥יו וְאֶת נָשָׁ֖יו עַל הַגְּמַלִּֽים

verses.restored: He drove all his livestock and all his possessions that he had gathered, the livestock of his acquisition that he had gathered in Paddan-Aram, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.

familiar.text: And he carried away all his cattle, and all his goods...

modern.text: and he drove all his livestock before him, along with all the possessions he had acquired in Paddan-aram, to go to his father Isaac in the land in Canaan.

original.text: וַיִּנְהַ֣ג אֶת כָּל מִקְנֵ֗הוּ וְאֶת כָּל רְכֻשׁוֹ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר רָכָ֔שׁ מִקְנֵה֙ קִנְיָנ֔וֹ אֲשֶׁ֥ר רָכַ֖שׁ בְּפַדַּ֣ן אֲרָ֑ם לָב֛וֹא אֶל יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִ֖יו אַ֥רְצָה כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: Laban had gone to shear his sheep, and Rachel stole the household gods that belonged to her father.

familiar.text: And Laban went to shear his sheep: and Rachel had stolen the images...

notes.title: Household gods
notes.body: Teraphim are household cult objects; Rachel’s motive is not stated.

modern.text: Now while Laban was out shearing his sheep, Rachel stole her father’s household idols.

original.text: וְלָבָ֣ן הָלַ֔ךְ לִגְזֹ֖ז אֶת צֹאנ֑וֹ וַתִּגְנֹ֣ב רָחֵ֔ל אֶת הַתְּרָפִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר לְאָבִֽיהָ

verses.restored: Jacob stole the heart of Laban the Aramean, by not telling him that he was fleeing.

familiar.text: And Jacob stole away unawares to Laban the Syrian...

notes.title: Stole the heart
notes.body: A Hebrew idiom meaning deceived or acted without informing.

modern.text: Moreover, Jacob deceived Laban the Aramean by not telling him that he was running away.

original.text: וַיִּגְנֹ֣ב יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶת לֵ֥ב לָבָ֖ן הָאֲרַמִּ֑י עַל בְּלִי֙ הִגִּ֣יד ל֔וֹ כִּ֥י בֹרֵ֖חַ הֽוּא

verses.restored: He fled with all that was his, rose, crossed the River, and set his face toward the hill country of Gilead.

familiar.text: So he fled with all that he had; and he rose up, and passed over the river...

modern.text: So he fled with all his possessions, crossed the Euphrates, and headed for the hill country of Gilead. Laban Pursues Jacob

original.text: וַיִּבְרַ֥ח הוּא֙ וְכָל אֲשֶׁר ל֔וֹ וַיָּ֖קָם וַיַּעֲבֹ֣ר אֶת הַנָּהָ֑ר וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֶת פָּנָ֖יו הַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: On the third day, Laban was told that Jacob had fled.

familiar.text: And it was told Laban on the third day that Jacob was fled.

modern.text: On the third day Laban was informed that Jacob had fled.

original.text: וַיֻּגַּ֥ד לְלָבָ֖ן בַּיּ֣וֹם הַשְּׁלִישִׁ֑י כִּ֥י בָרַ֖ח יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: He took his brothers with him and pursued him seven days’ journey, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

familiar.text: And he took his brethren with him, and pursued after him seven days' journey...

modern.text: So he took his relatives with him, pursued Jacob for seven days, and overtook him in the hill country of Gilead.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת אֶחָיו֙ עִמּ֔וֹ וַיִּרְדֹּ֣ף אַחֲרָ֔יו דֶּ֖רֶךְ שִׁבְעַ֣ת יָמִ֑ים וַיַּדְבֵּ֥ק אֹת֖וֹ בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: The Divine came to Laban the Aramean in a dream by night and said to him, Guard yourself, lest you speak with Jacob from good to bad.

familiar.text: And God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream by night...

notes.title: From good to bad
notes.body: An idiom warning Laban not to threaten or manipulate Jacob.

modern.text: But that night God came to Laban the Aramean in a dream and warned him, “Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.”

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֧א אֱלֹהִ֛ים אֶל לָבָ֥ן הָאֲרַמִּ֖י בַּחֲלֹ֣ם הַלָּ֑יְלָה וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ פֶּן תְּדַבֵּ֥ר עִֽם יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד רָֽע

verses.restored: Laban overtook Jacob. Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country, and Laban with his brothers pitched in the hill country of Gilead.

familiar.text: Then Laban overtook Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent...

modern.text: Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the hill country of Gilead when Laban overtook him, and Laban and his relatives camped there as well.

original.text: וַיַּשֵּׂ֥ג לָבָ֖ן אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב תָּקַ֤ע אֶֽת אָהֳלוֹ֙ בָּהָ֔ר וְלָבָ֛ן תָּקַ֥ע אֶת אֶחָ֖יו בְּהַ֥ר הַגִּלְעָֽד

verses.restored: Laban said to Jacob, What have you done? You stole my heart and drove my daughters away like captives of the sword.

familiar.text: And Laban said to Jacob, What hast thou done...

modern.text: Then Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done? You have deceived me and carried off my daughters like captives of war!

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר לָבָן֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב מֶ֣ה עָשִׂ֔יתָ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֶת לְבָבִ֑י וַתְּנַהֵג֙ אֶת בְּנֹתַ֔י כִּשְׁבֻי֖וֹת חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: Why did you flee secretly and steal me, and not tell me, so that I might have sent you away with joy and songs, with tambourine and lyre?

familiar.text: Wherefore didst thou flee away secretly, and steal away from me...

modern.text: Why did you run away secretly and deceive me, without even telling me? I would have sent you away with joy and singing, with tambourines and harps.

original.text: לָ֤מָּה נַחְבֵּ֨אתָ֙ לִבְרֹ֔חַ וַתִּגְנֹ֖ב אֹתִ֑י וְלֹא הִגַּ֣דְתָּ לִּ֔י וָֽאֲשַׁלֵּחֲךָ֛ בְּשִׂמְחָ֥ה וּבְשִׁרִ֖ים בְּתֹ֥ף וּבְכִנּֽוֹר

verses.restored: You did not allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters. Now you have acted foolishly.

familiar.text: And hast not suffered me to kiss my sons and my daughters?...

modern.text: But you did not even let me kiss my grandchildren and my daughters goodbye. Now you have done a foolish thing.

original.text: וְלֹ֣א נְטַשְׁתַּ֔נִי לְנַשֵּׁ֥ק לְבָנַ֖י וְלִבְנֹתָ֑י עַתָּ֖ה הִסְכַּ֥לְתָּֽ עֲשֽׂוֹ

verses.restored: It is in the power of my hand to do harm to you, but the Divine of your father spoke to me last night, saying, Guard yourself from speaking with Jacob from good to bad.

familiar.text: It is in the power of my hand to do you hurt...

modern.text: I have power to do you great harm, but last night the God of your father said to me, ‘Be careful not to say anything to Jacob, either good or bad.’

original.text: יֶשׁ לְאֵ֣ל יָדִ֔י לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת עִמָּכֶ֖ם רָ֑ע וֵֽאלֹהֵ֨י אֲבִיכֶ֜ם אֶ֣מֶשׁ אָמַ֧ר אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֗ר הִשָּׁ֧מֶר לְךָ֛ מִדַּבֵּ֥ר עִֽם יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִטּ֥וֹב עַד רָֽע

verses.restored: Now you have surely gone because you deeply longed for your father’s house. But why did you steal my gods?

familiar.text: And now, though thou wouldest needs be gone... wherefore hast thou stolen my gods?

modern.text: Now you have gone off because you long for your father’s house. But why have you stolen my gods?”

original.text: וְעַתָּה֙ הָלֹ֣ךְ הָלַ֔כְתָּ כִּֽי נִכְסֹ֥ף נִכְסַ֖פְתָּה לְבֵ֣ית אָבִ֑יךָ לָ֥מָּה גָנַ֖בְתָּ אֶת אֱלֹהָֽי

verses.restored: Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid, for I said, Lest you take your daughters from me by force.

familiar.text: And Jacob answered and said to Laban, Because I was afraid...

modern.text: “I was afraid,” Jacob answered, “for I thought you would take your daughters from me by force.

original.text: וַיַּ֥עַן יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֑ן כִּ֣י יָרֵ֔אתִי כִּ֣י אָמַ֔רְתִּי פֶּן תִּגְזֹ֥ל אֶת בְּנוֹתֶ֖יךָ מֵעִמִּֽי

verses.restored: With whomever you find your gods, he shall not live. Before our brothers, recognize what is yours with me and take it. Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen them.

familiar.text: With whomsoever thou findest thy gods, let him not live...

notes.title: Dangerous oath
notes.body: Jacob unknowingly places Rachel in danger with his words.

modern.text: If you find your gods with anyone here, he shall not live! In the presence of our relatives, see for yourself if anything is yours, and take it back.” For Jacob did not know that Rachel had stolen the idols.

original.text: עִ֠ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר תִּמְצָ֣א אֶת אֱלֹהֶיךָ֮ לֹ֣א יִֽחְיֶה֒ נֶ֣גֶד אַחֵ֧ינוּ הַֽכֶּר לְךָ֛ מָ֥ה עִמָּדִ֖י וְקַֽח לָ֑ךְ וְלֹֽא יָדַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב כִּ֥י רָחֵ֖ל גְּנָבָֽתַם

verses.restored: Laban went into Jacob’s tent, Leah’s tent, and the tent of the two slave-women, but he did not find them. He went out from Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.

familiar.text: And Laban went into Jacob's tent, and into Leah's tent...

modern.text: So Laban went into Jacob’s tent, then Leah’s tent, and then the tents of the two maidservants, but he found nothing. Then he left Leah’s tent and entered Rachel’s tent.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א לָבָ֜ן בְּאֹ֥הֶל יַעֲקֹ֣ב וּבְאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֗ה וּבְאֹ֛הֶל שְׁתֵּ֥י הָאֲמָהֹ֖ת וְלֹ֣א מָצָ֑א וַיֵּצֵא֙ מֵאֹ֣הֶל לֵאָ֔ה וַיָּבֹ֖א בְּאֹ֥הֶל רָחֵֽל

verses.restored: Rachel had taken the household gods and put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt through all the tent but did not find them.

familiar.text: Now Rachel had taken the images, and put them in the camel's furniture...

modern.text: Now Rachel had taken Laban’s household idols, put them in the saddlebag of her camel, and was sitting on them. And Laban searched everything in the tent but found nothing.

original.text: וְרָחֵ֞ל לָקְחָ֣ה אֶת הַתְּרָפִ֗ים וַתְּשִׂמֵ֛ם בְּכַ֥ר הַגָּמָ֖ל וַתֵּ֣שֶׁב עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיְמַשֵּׁ֥שׁ לָבָ֛ן אֶת כָּל הָאֹ֖הֶל וְלֹ֥א מָצָֽא

verses.restored: She said to her father, Let there be no anger in my lord’s eyes that I cannot rise before you, for the way of women is upon me. He searched but did not find the household gods.

familiar.text: And she said to her father, Let it not displease my lord that I cannot rise up...

modern.text: Rachel said to her father, “Sir, do not be angry that I cannot stand up before you; for I am having my period.” So Laban searched, but could not find the household idols.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל אָבִ֗יהָ אַל יִ֨חַר֙ בְּעֵינֵ֣י אֲדֹנִ֔י כִּ֣י ל֤וֹא אוּכַל֙ לָק֣וּם מִפָּנֶ֔יךָ כִּי דֶ֥רֶךְ נָשִׁ֖ים לִ֑י וַיְחַפֵּ֕שׂ וְלֹ֥א מָצָ֖א אֶת הַתְּרָפִֽים

verses.restored: Jacob became angry and argued with Laban. Jacob answered and said to Laban, What is my transgression? What is my offense, that you have hotly pursued me?

familiar.text: And Jacob was wroth, and chode with Laban...

modern.text: Then Jacob became incensed and challenged Laban. “What is my crime?” he said. “For what sin of mine have you so hotly pursued me?

original.text: וַיִּ֥חַר לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיָּ֣רֶב בְּלָבָ֑ן וַיַּ֤עַן יַעֲקֹב֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לְלָבָ֔ן מַה פִּשְׁעִי֙ מַ֣ה חַטָּאתִ֔י כִּ֥י דָלַ֖קְתָּ אַחֲרָֽי

verses.restored: Though you have felt through all my goods, what have you found from all the goods of your house? Set it here before my brothers and your brothers, and let them decide between us two.

familiar.text: Whereas thou hast searched all my stuff, what hast thou found...

modern.text: You have searched all my goods! Have you found anything that belongs to you? Put it here before my brothers and yours, that they may judge between the two of us.

original.text: כִּֽי מִשַּׁ֣שְׁתָּ אֶת כָּל כֵּלַ֗י מַה מָּצָ֨אתָ֙ מִכֹּ֣ל כְּלֵי בֵיתֶ֔ךָ שִׂ֣ים כֹּ֔ה נֶ֥גֶד אַחַ֖י וְאַחֶ֑יךָ וְיוֹכִ֖יחוּ בֵּ֥ין שְׁנֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: These twenty years I have been with you; your ewes and female goats have not miscarried, and the rams of your flock I have not eaten.

familiar.text: This twenty years have I been with thee; thy ewes and thy she goats...

modern.text: I have been with you for twenty years now. Your sheep and goats have not miscarried, nor have I eaten the rams of your flock.

original.text: זֶה֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים שָׁנָ֤ה אָנֹכִי֙ עִמָּ֔ךְ רְחֵלֶ֥יךָ וְעִזֶּ֖יךָ לֹ֣א שִׁכֵּ֑לוּ וְאֵילֵ֥י צֹאנְךָ֖ לֹ֥א אָכָֽלְתִּי

verses.restored: What was torn by beasts I did not bring to you; I bore the loss myself. From my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

familiar.text: That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee...

modern.text: I did not bring you anything torn by wild beasts; I bore the loss myself. And you demanded payment from me for what was stolen by day or night.

original.text: טְרֵפָה֙ לֹא הֵבֵ֣אתִי אֵלֶ֔יךָ אָנֹכִ֣י אֲחַטֶּ֔נָּה מִיָּדִ֖י תְּבַקְשֶׁ֑נָּה גְּנֻֽבְתִ֣י י֔וֹם וּגְנֻֽבְתִ֖י לָֽיְלָה

verses.restored: By day heat consumed me, and cold by night, and my sleep fled from my eyes.

familiar.text: Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night...

modern.text: As it was, the heat consumed me by day and the frost by night, and sleep fled from my eyes.

original.text: הָיִ֧יתִי בַיּ֛וֹם אֲכָלַ֥נִי חֹ֖רֶב וְקֶ֣רַח בַּלָּ֑יְלָה וַתִּדַּ֥ד שְׁנָתִ֖י מֵֽעֵינָֽי

verses.restored: These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flock, and you changed my wages ten times.

familiar.text: Thus have I been twenty years in thy house; I served thee fourteen years...

modern.text: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household—fourteen years for your two daughters and six years for your flocks—and you have changed my wages ten times!

original.text: זֶה לִּ֞י עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָה֮ בְּבֵיתֶךָ֒ עֲבַדְתִּ֜יךָ אַרְבַּֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֤ה שָׁנָה֙ בִּשְׁתֵּ֣י בְנֹתֶ֔יךָ וְשֵׁ֥שׁ שָׁנִ֖ים בְּצֹאנֶ֑ךָ וַתַּחֲלֵ֥ף אֶת מַשְׂכֻּרְתִּ֖י עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת מֹנִֽים

verses.restored: If the Divine of my father, the Divine of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. The Divine saw my affliction and the toil of my hands, and rebuked you last night.

familiar.text: Except the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac...

notes.title: Fear of Isaac
notes.body: A striking divine title tied to Isaac’s reverent awe or the God whom Isaac fears.

modern.text: If the God of my father, the God of Abraham and the Fear of Isaac, had not been with me, surely by now you would have sent me away empty-handed. But God has seen my affliction and the toil of my hands, and last night He rendered judgment.” Jacob’s Covenant with Laban

original.text: לוּלֵ֡י אֱלֹהֵ֣י אָבִי֩ אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וּפַ֤חַד יִצְחָק֙ הָ֣יָה לִ֔י כִּ֥י עַתָּ֖ה רֵיקָ֣ם שִׁלַּחְתָּ֑נִי אֶת עָנְיִ֞י וְאֶת יְגִ֧יעַ כַּפַּ֛י רָאָ֥ה אֱלֹהִ֖ים וַיּ֥וֹכַח אָֽמֶשׁ

verses.restored: Laban answered and said to Jacob, The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flock is my flock, and all that you see is mine. But what can I do today to these my daughters or to their children whom they have borne?

familiar.text: And Laban answered and said unto Jacob, These daughters are my daughters...

modern.text: But Laban answered Jacob, “These daughters are my daughters, these sons are my sons, and these flocks are my flocks! Everything you see is mine! Yet what can I do today about these daughters of mine or the children they have borne?

original.text: וַיַּ֨עַן לָבָ֜ן וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶֽל יַעֲקֹ֗ב הַבָּנ֨וֹת בְּנֹתַ֜י וְהַבָּנִ֤ים בָּנַי֙ וְהַצֹּ֣אן צֹאנִ֔י וְכֹ֛ל אֲשֶׁר אַתָּ֥ה רֹאֶ֖ה לִי ה֑וּא וְלִבְנֹתַ֞י מָֽה אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֤ה לָאֵ֨לֶּה֙ הַיּ֔וֹם א֥וֹ לִבְנֵיהֶ֖ן אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָלָֽדוּ

verses.restored: Now come, let us cut a covenant, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you.

familiar.text: Now therefore come thou, let us make a covenant, I and thou...

modern.text: Come now, let us make a covenant, you and I, and let it serve as a witness between you and me.”

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה לְכָ֛ה נִכְרְתָ֥ה בְרִ֖ית אֲנִ֣י וָאָ֑תָּה וְהָיָ֥ה לְעֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.

familiar.text: And Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

modern.text: So Jacob picked out a stone and set it up as a pillar,

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֥ח יַעֲקֹ֖ב אָ֑בֶן וַיְרִימֶ֖הָ מַצֵּבָֽה

verses.restored: Jacob said to his brothers, Gather stones. They took stones and made a heap, and they ate there by the heap.

familiar.text: And Jacob said unto his brethren, Gather stones...

modern.text: and he said to his relatives, “Gather some stones.” So they took stones and made a mound, and there by the mound they ate.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יַעֲקֹ֤ב לְאֶחָיו֙ לִקְט֣וּ אֲבָנִ֔ים וַיִּקְח֥וּ אֲבָנִ֖ים וַיַּֽעֲשׂוּ גָ֑ל וַיֹּ֥אכְלוּ שָׁ֖ם עַל הַגָּֽל

verses.restored: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.

familiar.text: And Laban called it Jegarsahadutha: but Jacob called it Galeed.

notes.title: Aramaic/Hebrew naming
notes.body: Both names mean heap of witness, one in Aramaic, one in Hebrew.

modern.text: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha, and Jacob called it Galeed.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָא ל֣וֹ לָבָ֔ן יְגַ֖ר שָׂהֲדוּתָ֑א וְיַֽעֲקֹ֔ב קָ֥רָא ל֖וֹ גַּלְעֵֽד

verses.restored: Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and you today. Therefore its name was called Galeed,

familiar.text: And Laban said, This heap is a witness between me and thee this day...

modern.text: Then Laban declared, “This mound is a witness between you and me this day.” Therefore the place was called Galeed.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָבָ֔ן הַגַּ֨ל הַזֶּ֥ה עֵ֛ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינְךָ֖ הַיּ֑וֹם עַל כֵּ֥ן קָרָֽא שְׁמ֖וֹ גַּלְעֵֽד

verses.restored: and Mizpah, for he said, May the Eternal watch between me and you when we are hidden from each other.

familiar.text: And Mizpah; for he said, The LORD watch between me and thee...

notes.title: Mizpah
notes.body: Often quoted sentimentally, but here it functions as a boundary-watch between mistrustful parties.

modern.text: It was also called Mizpah, because Laban said, “May the LORD keep watch between you and me when we are absent from each other.

original.text: וְהַמִּצְפָּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָמַ֔ר יִ֥צֶף יְהוָ֖ה בֵּינִ֣י וּבֵינֶ֑ךָ כִּ֥י נִסָּתֵ֖ר אִ֥ישׁ מֵרֵעֵֽהוּ

verses.restored: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take women besides my daughters, though no one is with us, see, the Divine is witness between me and you.

familiar.text: If thou shalt afflict my daughters, or if thou shalt take other wives beside my daughters...

modern.text: If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, although no one is with us, remember that God is a witness between you and me.”

original.text: אִם תְּעַנֶּ֣ה אֶת בְּנֹתַ֗י וְאִם תִּקַּ֤ח נָשִׁים֙ עַל בְּנֹתַ֔י אֵ֥ין אִ֖ישׁ עִמָּ֑נוּ רְאֵ֕ה אֱלֹהִ֥ים עֵ֖ד בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Laban said to Jacob, Look at this heap, and look at the pillar that I have set between me and you.

familiar.text: And Laban said to Jacob, Behold this heap, and behold this pillar...

modern.text: Laban also said to Jacob, “Here is the mound, and here is the pillar I have set up between you and me.

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן לְיַעֲקֹ֑ב הִנֵּ֣ה הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֗ה וְהִנֵּה֙ הַמַצֵּבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר יָרִ֖יתִי בֵּינִ֥י וּבֵינֶֽךָ

verses.restored: This heap is witness, and the pillar is witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

familiar.text: This heap be witness, and this pillar be witness...

modern.text: This mound is a witness, and this pillar is a witness, that I will not go past this mound to harm you, and you will not go past this mound and pillar to harm me.

original.text: עֵ֚ד הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְעֵדָ֖ה הַמַּצֵּבָ֑ה אִם אָ֗נִי לֹֽא אֶֽעֱבֹ֤ר אֵלֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶת הַגַּ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה וְאִם אַ֠תָּה לֹא תַעֲבֹ֨ר אֵלַ֜י אֶת הַגַּ֥ל הַזֶּ֛ה וְאֶת הַמַּצֵּבָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְרָעָֽה

verses.restored: May the Divine of Abraham and the divine of Nahor judge between us, the divine of their father. Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

familiar.text: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge betwixt us...

notes.title: Different divine references
notes.body: The verse preserves the complexity of ancestral divine language; Jacob swears by the Fear of Isaac.

modern.text: May the God of Abraham and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” So Jacob swore by the Fear of his father Isaac.

original.text: אֱלֹהֵ֨י אַבְרָהָ֜ם וֵֽאלֹהֵ֤י נָחוֹר֙ יִשְׁפְּט֣וּ בֵינֵ֔ינוּ אֱלֹהֵ֖י אֲבִיהֶ֑ם וַיִּשָּׁבַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב בְּפַ֖חַד אָבִ֥יו יִצְחָֽק

verses.restored: Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and called his brothers to eat bread. They ate bread and spent the night on the mountain.

familiar.text: Then Jacob offered sacrifice upon the mount, and called his brethren to eat bread...

modern.text: Then Jacob offered a sacrifice on the mountain and invited his relatives to eat a meal. And after they had eaten, they spent the night on the mountain.

original.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֨ח יַעֲקֹ֥ב זֶ֨בַח֙ בָּהָ֔ר וַיִּקְרָ֥א לְאֶחָ֖יו לֶאֱכָל לָ֑חֶם וַיֹּ֣אכְלוּ לֶ֔חֶם וַיָּלִ֖ינוּ בָּהָֽר

verses.restored: Early in the morning Laban rose, kissed his sons and daughters, and blessed them. Then Laban went and returned to his place.

familiar.text: And early in the morning Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters...

modern.text: Early the next morning, Laban got up and kissed his grandchildren and daughters and blessed them. Then he left to return home.

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם לָבָ֜ן בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיְנַשֵּׁ֧ק לְבָנָ֛יו וְלִבְנוֹתָ֖יו וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֶתְהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֛לֶךְ וַיָּ֥שָׁב לָבָ֖ן לִמְקֹמֽוֹ
